title: The college cafeteria
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The college has a cafeteria. Adults in it, facing every direction. Wood sits at the near end of a long table. The strip doesn't say what this rhymes with.

panels.composition: A community college cafeteria at noon: round tables, adults of every age facing every direction, a vending machine, a window on the lot. WOOD at the near end of the one long table.

image.prompt: a community college cafeteria at noon with round tables of adults of all ages facing every direction, a young man alone at the end of one long table by the window, black and white, no words

panels.composition: His tray. Corn. He didn't choose it; it came.

image.prompt: close on a cafeteria tray with a paper cup of corn kernels and a plastic fork, black and white, no words

panels.composition: A CLASSMATE, fifty, in a mill jacket, sitting down across from him without asking. Eating.

balloons.text: You're the one with the booklet.

image.prompt: an older man in a faded mill jacket sitting down across from a young man at a cafeteria table, both eating, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The long table from the far end. Two men at the near end, facing each other. Everyone else facing everywhere. The strip lets the rhyme go.

image.prompt: a long cafeteria table seen from its far end with two men at the near end facing each other while the room faces every direction, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Nobody faces one direction here. Corn anyway. #1 is not quoted.
